text:
ashley: Hey team — customer reported 401s only when bundling our Node SDK with webpack in an SSR build. Works fine in plain node. Repro steps below, curious if anyone has seen ESM/CJS entry weirdness.

ashley: repro: Next.js serverless build -> webpack 5 -> app imports `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` -> runtime throws 401 from fetch to /v1 . If I change import to `require('redwood-sdk')` on the same server it works.

ashley: bundle info: node 18, next 13.4, webpack 5, redwood-sdk@2.0.1. vendor uses esbuild for client.

devon: hmmm. do you have the bundle output (server) that shows which entry field webpack resolved? often bundlers prefer "module" over "main" and we ship ESM shims that don't include the auth shim for SSR.

ashley: attaching minimal webpack trace: `resolved redwood-sdk -> /node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/esm/index.js`

samir: quick thought: our CJS build includes a small auth header shim for server-side fetch retries. the ESM build expects global fetch to be configured differently. if webpack picks ESM it might not include the node-specific adapter.

ashley: yeah that matches. customer said other libs behave the same. any recommended short-term workaround we can tell them?

devon: workarounds I've used: 1) force resolve to cjs entry by aliasing: `resolve.alias: { 'redwood-sdk$': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/cjs/index.js') }` 2) set `resolve.mainFields = ['main', 'module']` so main (CJS) wins on server bundle 3) import the CJS subpath explicitly: `const Redwood = require('redwood-sdk/dist/cjs')`. all messy but effective.

samir: long term we should publish a clearer dual-entrypoint in package.json exports to make bundlers pick the CJS entry for server builds. Also add an `exports."./server"` stub that points to cjs. I can open a PR.

ashley: can we also add a note in docs about Next/webpack SSR gotchas? customer hit this in prod.

devon: yes, doc + changelog entry. For this sprint I'm adding a compatibility test in our CI: webpack + next server bundle should import and preserve server auth headers.

build-bot: deploy-job #1284: triggered by samir/exports-pr, CI runs 8/12 tests passing locally — failing test: "ssr-auth-headers"

samir: I'm going to reproduce locally with minimal Next server build and try both 2.0.1 and 1.9.8 to see when the behavior changed. initial guess: we started publishing a pure esm `module` field in v2 and some packagers started preferring it.

ashley: customer asked if pinning to older version is safe. devon?

devon: short answer: yes, pin to 1.9.x until we cut a compatibility patch. but warn them 1.9.x lacks some new runtime perf fixes. ideally apply the alias workaround until we release 2.0.2 with a server entry.

ashley: noted. I'll send the alias snippet + explicit require option to customer, mention pin to 1.9.x and ETA for fix.

samir: created issue #412: "packaging: provide explicit server cjs export to avoid bundler ESM resolution causing auth gaps" and linked PR draft.

devon: thanks — tagging @eng-runtime to prioritize the PR for next patch release. :thumbsup:

ashley: thanks all — closing this thread after I confirm customer can patch.
